title: Mount Manipur National Park
subtitle: Formerly Mount Harriet National Park
overview: Mount Manipur is the third highest peak in the Andaman Islands, located in South Andaman. Rich in biodiversity, scenic beauty, and historical significance, it was renamed to honor the freedom fighters from Manipur who were exiled here during British rule. It is famous for its dense tropical forests, endemic flora and fauna, and colonial-era history.

title: Wright Myo Creek
subtitle: Ferrargunj, South Andaman

Managed by the Andaman Forest Department as an eco-tourism initiative, it offers peaceful nature immersion about 48 km from Port Blair

accessibility.ship: By Ship: From Port Blair, one must take a ferry to Chatham Jetty → Bamboo Flat Jetty → then a road trip to the Wright Myo Creek.

title: Loha Barrack Crocodile Wildlife Sanctuary
subtitle: South Andaman
rangeDivision: Loha Barrack Wildlife Sanctuary Range Wildlife Division Haddo
overview: Located on the western coast of South Andaman Island, the sanctuary was officially declared in 1983 to protect the estuarine–mangrove habitat of the saltwater crocodile (Crocodylus porosus). Named for the adjacent village of Lohabarrack, over 91% of its area comprises marine and mangrove ecosystems, making it the only protected area among 96 in the region specifically for crocodile conservation. A comprehensive survey recorded 146 species of scleractinian corals here, underscoring its marine biodiversity significance

permits: Visitors must obtain a Forest Department permit from the Department of Environment & Forests office in Port Blair or from the ranger check-post at Lohabarrack. A local guide (mandatory) will typically organize this on your behalf

They are nestled amidst dense tropical forests and mangroves, offering a unique experience in the heart of Andaman.

title: Mud Volcano
subtitle: Baratang Island
overview: The Mud Volcano in Baratang Island is a rare geological phenomenon found in only a few places around the world. It is not a typical lava volcano but instead releases mud, gases like methane, and water. The eruptions are slow, and the site offers a unique opportunity to witness nature’s forces in a subtler form. It is an important part of the island’s natural heritage.

title: Cuthbert Bay Beach & Wildlife Sanctuary
subtitle: Rangat Island
overview: Cuthbert Bay Beach is a long, pristine stretch of golden sand on the eastern coast of Middle Andaman, renowned as one of the most important marine turtle nesting grounds in the Andaman & Nicobar archipelago. The adjacent Cuthbert Bay Wildlife Sanctuary (5.8 km², established 1997) protects nesting sites of Olive Ridley, Leatherback and Green turtles, as well as resident deer, birds and butterflies

accessibility.ship: By Sea: Regular government ferries and private boats run from Port Blair to Rangat (approx. 4–6 hours) via the Grand Andaman Trunk Road ferry service

bestTime: Turtle Nesting Season: December through February, when hundreds of marine turtles come ashore to lay eggs Off-Peak Months: March–May for quieter beaches and moderate weather; monsoon (June–September) sees heavy rains and rough seas.

title: Uttara Jetty
subtitle: Baratang Island, Middle Andaman
overview: Uttara Jetty serves as the primary embarkation point for visitors heading to the famed Limestone Caves and the Mud Volcano on Baratang Island. Situated across the strait from Baratang Jetty, it facilitates boat transfers through a narrow mangrove‐lined channel before opening into the Bay of Bengal. The jetty platform has been extended to 200 m to accommodate larger vessels, ensuring year‐round connectivity for passenger launches and supply boats.

accessibility.road: By Road & Convoy: From Port Blair, it’s a ~110 km journey via NH4 through Jarawa tribal reserve, taking about 4½–5 hours. Private cars, taxis or government buses (departing at ~5:30 AM and 11:00 AM) must join regulated convoys at designated check posts.

title: Mud Volcanoes of Shyamnagar
subtitle: “Jal Tikry”, Diglipur
overview: A rare geological phenomenon, this chain of small mud volcanoes is formed by the upwelling of subsurface mud and gases. Scattered across a clearing in the semi-evergreen forest of Shyamnagar, you’ll find one larger, often dormant vent and several smaller, intermittently bubbling craters—truly a glimpse into the island’s dynamic subsoil processes

Known for its black rocks ("Kala Pathar" translates to "Black Rock" in Hindi), turquoise waters, and lush greenery, it's an ideal location for nature lovers seeking peace and raw natural beauty. It remains largely untouched and less commercialized compared to other beaches in the archipelago.

accessibility.road: By Road: Once at Hut Bay, Kalapathar Beach can be accessed by local road transport (jeeps, motorbikes for hire). The beach is approximately 14 km from Hut Bay.
accessibility.ship: By Ship: Reach Little Andaman from Port Blair by government-run ferries (approx. 6–8 hours). Ships operate from Phoenix Bay Jetty, Port Blair to Hut Bay Jetty in Little Andaman.

bestTime: Season: November to April Calm seas, pleasant weather, and clear skies enhance beach exploration and activities.
timing: Open throughout the day, but best visited during daylight hours (6:00 AM to 5:00 PM) for safety and to enjoy natural light.
permits: Indian nationals do not require special permits to visit Little Andaman. Foreign nationals require Restricted Area Permits (RAP), which are available upon arrival at Port Blair or through Indian embassies abroad.
fees: No entry fee for Kalapathar Beach. Charges may apply for hiring vehicles or guides.
activities: Exploring black rock formations (Note: Swimming is not recommended due to sharp rocks and unpredictable waves.)
facility: Basic facilities only:
No food stalls or changing rooms near the beach
Carry drinking water, snacks, and essentials
Dustbins are limited – carry back your waste
accommodation: Limited options available in Hut Bay and surrounding villages Government guest houses and a few budget private lodges Advance booking is advised during the tourist season
hospital: Primary Health Centre (PHC) available at Hut Bay For major treatments, one must travel back to Port Blair (by ship or helicopter in emergencies)

conservationNotes: Kalapathar Beach is part of a fragile coastal ecosystem. Coral reefs and coastal flora are vulnerable to human activity. Avoid touching or stepping on coral or disturbing wildlife.
